# v1.1.0-dev.65 — The editor stops showing you a stale list

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.64`.

Bug fix release. Registering a resolution with a virtual display
appeared to do nothing. The only way to see it was to restart the
app.

## What Was Wrong

The Display editor read every display's resolution list once, when
you opened it, and never looked again. Nothing told it when your
displays changed either.

So the exact sequence the feature is built around fell over. You
register a size, you reconnect the display so the driver picks it
up, you go back to the editor, and it shows you the list from
before the reconnect. The resolution really was there. The app just
wasn't looking.

Restarting WLM fixed it, which is a terrible way to find out.

## What Happens Now

The editor re-reads whenever Windows reports a display change. A
virtual display reconnecting now updates the list while you're
looking at it. Registering a resolution re-reads too.

Anything you'd already picked and not yet saved stays picked. The
editor doesn't fetch at all while it's closed.

## The By-Hand Message Was A Dead End

Typing a size the driver doesn't list yet got you this:

```
This display does not offer this mode yet.
```

True, and no help at all. On a virtual display there's a specific
next step. It isn't guessable. Now it says what it is:

```
This display does not offer this mode yet. Add it with the
"Add resolutions" button below, then reconnect the display. It is
saved either way, and applies as soon as the driver lists it.
```

A driver WLM can't write to gets that driver's own instructions
instead. A physical monitor keeps the plain wording, because there
the cause is something else.

The "saved either way" part was always true and never said. A size
your display can't do yet is kept in the profile and applies the
moment the driver starts offering it.

## Still Open

On the machine that reported this, the two registry slots WLM
writes are missing even though the administrator prompt was
approved. Every part of that write path checks out where it can be
tested. This is unreproduced rather than fixed.

WLM now records the outcome of each registration attempt. If it
happens again there's something to read.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
